stem: Why is cation-exchange capacity relevant when evaluating a root-zone medium?
choices: It estimates how rapidly oxygen moves through the medium, which determines how efficiently roots can exchange gases during irrigation cycles
It describes a medium's ability to retain and exchange positively charged ions, which can influence nutrient buffering and availability
It measures the total dissolved-ion concentration of the root zone and therefore serves as a substrate-specific form of electrical conductivity
It describes how strongly the medium resists changes in water content, which is why higher values indicate greater moisture-buffering capacity
rationale: Cation-exchange capacity describes the capacity of a medium to hold and exchange cations. It can influence how nutrients are retained and buffered in the root zone.
